title: Negroponte
capsule: Negroponte (Euboea) was carved out of Byzantine territory after the Fourth Crusade's sack of Constantinople in 1204 and initially divided among three Lombard lords—the so-called Triarchy—who held it as vassals of the Latin Empire. In the years 1206–1210 this triarchic arrangement was being consolidated, with Venice asserting a supervising role as bailiff of the island that would eventually give it dominant influence. The island's strategic position in the Aegean made it a major commercial and naval hub, remaining under nominal Venetian suzerainty for over two centuries until the Ottoman conquest of 1470.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political structure of Negroponte in 1206–1210 is attested in crusader chronicles and Venetian records, but the precise territorial boundaries of individual lordships within the island at this early stage are not well mapped.
